Variants.Content: Apulum fields, herds and Danube exchange feed followers. Roman markets and local stores both matter; long assembly reduces household surplus.

Apulum fields, herds and Danube exchange sustain followers. Traveling followers need real food from this production; valuables still require a buyer and exchange. Roman markets and local stores both support Thervingian livelihoods.

Roman markets and local stores both support Thervingian livelihoods. Collectors and distributors depend on the next yield too; extra demands leave losses with continuing suppliers. Apulum fields, herds and Danube exchange sustain followers.
